parsed.main_gap: Self-duality (hypothesis (iii)) is verified only for finite minimal transversals (via π(T)), yet Step 4's decisive contradiction applies it to a minimal transversal inside the infinite set I∪Z_ω.

errors.description: Claim 3.2 proves self-duality only when the minimal transversal T of C is finite, since it forms the integer π(T) and uses membership in S_∞. But in Step 4 the final contradiction extracts (by Zorn) a minimal transversal inside the infinite set I∪Z_ω, which is not known to be finite; indeed Case A being impossible at every stage shows no finite I∪Z_s is a transversal, so the weaker finite version cannot be substituted. Load-bearing gap.
errors.quote: Hence $\pi(T)\in S_\infty$, so $\pi(T)$ is a multiple of some $\pi(t')$ with $t'\in\mathcal C$

parsed.notes: Steps 1–2 (reduction to finiteness of minimal elements) and Claim 3.1 are correct and clean; the combinatorial core theorem's peeling/least-index argument is valid given hypothesis (iii) in the strong (infinite) form. Only the verification of (iii) in that strength is missing.
